title: Fictional Vehicle Digital Access Specification — Educational Demo Only
disclaimer: Entirely independently authored hypothetical requirements. NOT CCC Digital Key Specification, NOT actual 3.1.4 or 4.1.0 requirements, and not evidence of compliance. Version labels V1/V2 are fictional.

requirements.heading: Owner Device Provisioning
requirements.text: In this fictional protocol, a vehicle SHALL create an owner-device record only after a local enrollment challenge and a second owner confirmation step are completed.

requirements.heading: Offline Initial Pairing
requirements.text: If the fictional vehicle is offline, initial owner pairing MAY proceed using a locally issued enrollment token, provided that the token has not expired; cloud synchronization SHALL wait until connectivity returns.

requirements.heading: Friend Key Sharing
requirements.text: A fictional owner device MAY issue a friend-device invitation only when sharing is enabled, an explicit entitlement set is assigned, and the invitation expiration time is recorded.

requirements.heading: Delegated Sharing
requirements.text: In this fictional V2 profile, a friend device MAY create a single delegated invitation only if the owner explicitly enables delegation and the delegated entitlements are a subset of the friend's entitlements; further delegation SHALL NOT be permitted.

requirements.heading: Key Revocation
requirements.text: After a fictional key is marked revoked, the access controller SHALL reject subsequent operations using that credential and any invitations derived from it, even if radio authentication succeeds.

requirements.heading: Temporary Suspension
requirements.text: The fictional owner MAY temporarily suspend a friend credential. Suspension SHALL also block delegated credentials until an owner-approved resume event is completed.

requirements.heading: BLE Discovery
requirements.text: For this fictional demo, BLE discovery MAY indicate a nearby vehicle, but an access session SHALL proceed only after an explicit device capability check; discovery SHALL NOT grant access.

requirements.heading: BLE Connection Failure
requirements.text: If a fictional BLE connection attempt times out, the mobile device MAY retry up to two times with backoff; it SHALL NOT report success without the authenticated session state.

requirements.heading: UWB Passive Entry
requirements.text: When passive entry is enabled, the fictional vehicle SHALL verify an active credential, the requested operation entitlement, an authenticated session, and an acceptable UWB range before unlocking.

requirements.heading: Ranging Unavailable
requirements.text: If fictional UWB ranging is unavailable or confidence is insufficient, passive entry SHALL stop. The user MAY attempt NFC tap-to-access only when the credential permits NFC entry.

requirements.heading: NFC Tap-to-Access
requirements.text: For fictional NFC entry, a valid credential and explicit tap SHALL be verified; NFC access SHALL NOT depend on a prior UWB session, but a suspended credential SHALL be rejected.

requirements.heading: Operation Entitlements
requirements.text: Every fictional access request SHALL be checked against the credential's allowed operations and channel restrictions. Entry-only or NFC-only permission SHALL NOT imply vehicle-start permission.

requirements.heading: Time-Limited Access
requirements.text: When a fictional shared credential has an active-time window, the vehicle SHALL reject access outside that window, including for delegated invitations, regardless of radio discovery success.

requirements.heading: Offline Operation
requirements.text: While the fictional vehicle is offline, previously activated local credentials MAY be checked, but delegated invitations and changes to entitlements SHALL require an updated approval record.

requirements.heading: Minimal Event Logging
requirements.text: For fictional audit trails, the system SHALL record an event category, result, and a short-lived pseudonymous correlation ID, while SHALL NOT export raw device identifiers with normal diagnostics.

requirements.heading: User-Facing Error
requirements.text: A fictional client SHALL distinguish 'credential revoked or suspended', 'proximity not verified', and 'radio unavailable' as separate error categories without revealing secret keys.

requirements.heading: Purpose and Scope
requirements.text: In this fictional specification, a digital key is a credential stored on a mobile device, such as a smartphone, that lets an authorized user unlock, lock, or start a vehicle without a physical key. This document is an independently authored educational demo, not an official specification.

requirements.heading: Feature Summary
requirements.text: This fictional digital key covers owner device provisioning (2.1), friend key sharing and delegation (2.2), revocation and suspension (2.3), BLE discovery, UWB passive entry and NFC tap-to-access (3.x), operation entitlements and time limits (4.1), offline operation (4.2), and privacy-preserving logging and error reporting (5.x).

requirements.heading: Terms
requirements.text: In this fictional document, an owner device is the first device provisioned for a vehicle; a friend device receives a shared key from the owner; a credential is the key data a device presents; an entitlement is an allowed operation such as entry or start; passive entry unlocks the vehicle when an authorized device is verified nearby without a user action.

requirements.heading: Changes from V1
requirements.text: Compared with the fictional V1 profile, V2 adds a second owner confirmation during provisioning (2.1.1), expiring enrollment tokens and invitations (2.1.2, 2.2.1), owner-controlled single-level delegation (2.2.2), a device capability check after BLE discovery (3.1.1), up to two BLE retries with backoff (3.1.2), channel-restricted entitlements such as NFC-only (4.1.1), pseudonymous correlation IDs in logs (5.1.1), and more specific user-facing error categories (5.2.1).
